outcome.technical: drive-phase.py. RULE A: skills_at_commit (its own ls-tree/cat-file reading of git objects, the posixpath import with it) and _copy_words are removed. checkout_at(ctx, commit) makes a detached checkout with `git worktree add --detach --quiet <mkdtemp(prefix=drive-pin-checkout-)>/tree <commit>` (the operation task-add cuts a member's tree with), a git refusal being a PinStop naming the commit; drop_checkout removes it through remove_base_tree (same holder/tree layout, the one removal question tree_unsettled asked first, worktree remove --force --force, rmtree), warning if anything is left. ask_member_pins makes ONE checkout per ask only when the plan pins (skill_pins not None) and a session-route member has no tree, asks every uncut member over member_project(checkout), and drops it in a finally (KeyboardInterrupt included); it no longer calls _areas.resolve_skills itself, so its _HANDOUT_EXEMPT row is gone. Git processes per ask: 3 with pins and an uncut member (worktree add, the removal question's rev-parse --git-dir, worktree remove), 0 for a plan with no pins, a cut member or the subagent route (spd31); the commit reader it replaced started 2 (ls-tree, cat-file) and no checkout. What a member tree gets after git (.worktreeinclude copies, setup) is not in the checkout - stated in the docstring and SECURITY.md. RULE C: one builder, pin_stop_words(exc, names, manifest, where, how) + _copy_remedy(verdict, tier, how): on a stop over a commit or tree copy it re-asks _skill_places.pin_stops over the same copy and, per stopped skill, takes the tier from resolve_skill(...)['source']; a project skill gets _STOP_REMEDY REPLACED (commit: 'That copy is commit <12>'s ... Restore the pinned bytes and COMMIT them, or <reader's re-pin tail>'; tree: 'That copy is the member's own tree ... Restore the pinned bytes there, not in the project, or <tail>'); personal, plugin and not-found keep the reader's words; the checkout path is renamed 'commit <12>'. ask_pins() is the drive's one call of require_pins (session_skills, runner_review_skill), session_skills/session_hand take `how`, hand_in_tree passes ('tree', tree). RULE B fix: validation_step no longer writes redispatched/asked before validation_dispatch; validation_dispatch(again=True) counts the re-dispatch in the same write as the ids, after its pins. LOW 5: drive's except BaseException arm gives the lock back only if lock_to_give_back(E_STOPPED, ...) says so; a rule that raises (the plan read failing again) keeps the lock, as an unreadable plan does on a return, and the original exception surfaces. tests/test_drive_phase.py (written first): the hand-kept _PIN_ASKS/_PIN_STARTS/_PIN_LOCKS/_STOP_ROUTES and _stop_route_functions/_route_verdict are replaced by a call-graph derivation (_pin_graph, _pin_routes: transitive over callers, seeded by raises of PinStop and calls into modules whose functions can raise it - _pin_stop_raisers, to a fixpoint) reduced by _STOP_ROUTES_EXEMPT (each row a reason and the callers it allows; stale and via checked both ways); _pin_blind_spots fails on a route used as a value, a lambda over one, getattr on a module holding a stop, globals/vars/locals/eval/exec/__import__ and sys.modules, with exactly two listed in _PIN_BLIND_LISTED; a PEP 578 audit-hook runtime record (_audit_hook/_record_*/_early_writes) on every scenario fails a write made before the first stop and not put back; _kept_state adds every phase field and git's HEAD/refs/packed-refs/worktrees (_git_kept). spd1's verdict now accepts reaching the reader through the module's own calls (_reader_reach). dl6 now holds both halves of low 5. spn-block 44/44 and dl-block 10/10 on this tree; final tests over the committed driver: spn-block 33/44 (red: spd1, spd2, spd22, spd23, spd24, spd25b, spd28, spd30, spd31, spd32, spd33, each by assertion), dl-block 9/10 (dl6). spd24a (the record's power) and spd24b (the validation allow twin) are green there by construction. Whole suite through the sweep: 1099 cases, exit 0.
